title: Private Deployments — Ops Scrub & Knowledge Transfer (Week of 2026-07-06)
content: Purpose: weekly operational scrub for private deployments (VPC + on-prem). This doc captures progress, outstanding customer blockers, and knowledge-transfer items we want to land in the runbook before next sprint. Tone: working notes; action-first; assume reader is an engineer on-call or in solutions.
high_level_summary: 1) Three active installs in parallel (AcadiaHealth VPC, FinEdge on-prem OVA, RetailCo air-gapped). 2) Primary recurring blocker is customer network misconfiguration (MTU/caps, proxy bypass, incorrect routes). 3) Two runbook items identified for immediate inclusion: KV cache /dev/shm sizing and AWS PrivateLink troubleshooting checklist. 4) Need SRE pairing for live packet captures on AcadiaHealth tomorrow.
notes:
Agenda:
- Quick state rollups for each active customer
- Triage new blockers and assign owners
- Runbook updates / knowledge transfer items
- Decisions & follow-ups

Customer: AcadiaHealth (hosted in customer VPC, AWS us-east-1)
- Current status: infra provisioning complete; control-plane nodes reporting but intermittent agent heartbeat failures.
- Symptom: intermittent 10-30s agent disconnects; subsequent reconnects cause KV cache warm restarts and spike in token latency.
- Recent debug: packet captures (tcpdump) on their ENI show occasional ICMP fragmentation needed messages and MSS lowered on TCP handshakes.
- Investigation hypothesis: MTU mismatch between customer VPC and their transit gateway + NAT behavior for egress to Redwood endpoints.
- Temporary mitigation: reduce instance MTU to 1400 on the control plane nodes (Samuel applied on one node -> agent stabilized).
- Long-term: schedule network design call with Acadia network team, propose PrivateLink or TransitGateway config change; SRE to assist with full pcap capture next Tuesday.
- Tickets: JIRA-PRIV-4721 (network-MTU-investigation), linked Confluence design draft attached.

Customer: FinEdge (on-prem OVA inside customer datacenter)
- Current status: OVA deploy completed; kubelet failing to register due to CRI socket permission mismatch.
- Symptom: installer logs show "failed to connect to /var/run/containerd/containerd.sock: permission denied" on first boot.
- Root cause: distribution image defaults to systemd-private for container runtime; our installer assumes containerd socket group is 'docker' (legacy).
- Fix applied: modified post-install script to chown containerd.sock and added SELinux boolean toggle for container runtime. Tested on staging image version 2026-06-28 and validated node registration.
- Next step: push patch to private-deploy-configs (PR #198) and coordinate patch release with FinEdge schedule.

Customer: RetailCo (air-gapped / high compliance)
- Current status: image transfer in progress; baseline install passed but smoke tests failing on time sync.
- Symptom: services show jittered timestamps (~4-7s drift) causing cert validation failures during mutual TLS handshake with Redwood control-plane endpoints (when in proxy-mode).
- Investigation: customer environment lacks NTP push; their local time source had leap-second offset.
- Mitigation: provided simple chrony config fragment and repair procedure; scheduled a non-peak maintenance window to apply fixes and rotate certs.

Runbook & knowledge transfer items (identified this scrub)
- Add "MTU and fragmentation" troubleshooting section with: how to capture pcap on ENI, interpreting ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages, recommended MTU fallbacks (1400), and when to recommend PrivateLink vs TransitGateway.
- Add "OVA post-install checks" checklist: verify CRI socket permissions, SELinux flags, /dev/shm size (>= 256MB for KV cache), sufficient ulimit for file descriptors, and swap disabled.
- Add "air-gapped TLS rotation" recipe: offline cert generation steps, double-check SANs, stub process for orchestrating cert swap with zero downtime.
- Add quick commands for on-call to gather telemetry (single-line copy-paste): systemctl status redwood-agent; journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 500; ss -tn sport = :443; sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/packets.pcap 'tcp and (port 443 or port 50051)'; df -h /dev/shm.

Decisions made
- We will standardize the OVA post-install script in the 2026-07-12 release; any hotfixes go through the private-deploy-configs PR flow. Owner: Marcus Chen.
- For AcadiaHealth, do not change production MTU cluster-wide without agreeing with their network team. Apply node-level workaround where needed and schedule design review. Owner: Aisha & Lena.
- Push the MTU troubleshooting doc into Confluence by Friday. Owner: Samuel.

Action items (owner + due):
action_items: Samuel: Draft MTU troubleshooting doc + pcap examples in Confluence (due 2026-07-10)
Lena: Pair with Acadia network team to capture full-day packet captures and assist with diagnosis (meeting 2026-07-08)
Marcus: Merge OVA post-install fixes into private-deploy-configs and tag a staging release (PR #198) (due 2026-07-11)
Priya: Coordinate RetailCo maintenance window and confirm cert rotation schedule (due 2026-07-09)
Aisha: Create escalation play for persistent agent reconnects (if >3 occurrences in 24h escalate to SRE pager) (due 2026-07-12)
blocking_questions_and_parking_lot:
1) Should we make 1400 MTU our default fallback in the installer for cloud/on-prem hybrid? Pros: reduces fragmentation issues; Cons: performance penalty for some networks. Need perf/benchmark.
2) Should the runbook include a small troubleshooting container that customers can run (tcpdump + journal upload) to simplify collection? Security review needed.
3) Can we add a small telemetry flag to the agent to emit MTU negotiation metrics (would help detect early)? Track as RFC.

Parking lot: formalize PrivateLink runbook; add recommended IAM/policy snippets for TransitGateway peering to Confluence.
appendix:
Useful commands collected during meeting:
- gather agent logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -o short-iso --no-pager | tail -n 500 > /tmp/agent.log
- basic net checks: ip link show; ip route show; sudo ethtool -k eth0 | head
- pcap for quick repro: sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/repro.pcap 'icmp or tcp' & sleep 30; sudo pkill tcpdump
- check /dev/shm: df -h /dev/shm
- quick cert inspect: openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.internal:443 -servername control.redwood.internal < /dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -text

References and links:
- Private Deploy Runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Private+Deploy+Runbook
- OVA staging image used: staging-ova-2026-06-28 (bucket link in Confluence)
- PR with post-install fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-configs/pull/198

Next meeting: ops scrub + dry-run checklist review on 2026-07-13 09:00 PT.

Notes capture author: Aisha Patel (additions by Marcus and Lena during live scrub).
final_note: This doc is intended to be ephemeral working notes — once MTU and OVA fixes are merged, we will consolidate the finalized steps into the canonical Private Deploy Runbook (Confluence). Keep this doc for traceability until next scrub.
